## Verdict
REVISE — The approach is viable, but paint gating, color resolution and deployment details need tightening.

## Critical gaps
- `render.go:108–114,204` collects pane rectangles only when existing backgrounds are enabled; both compositor paths similarly gate fill construction. Tint must work independently when every existing background option is off.
- Default backgrounds have no RGB value, and ANSI slots may use host-specific colors. Specify baseline resolution and unknown-color behavior; cache invalidation must include relevant ground, theme, host-palette and depth changes—not just focus/tint/strength.

## Important improvements
- Resolve reverse-video semantics: changing only `Style.Bg` while retaining `AttrReverse` changes visible foreground. Define the exception or effective-color policy.
- Apply tint after ordinary surface filling, without reusing foreground-adjusting behavior or changing OSC color reports.
- Regeneration must update the installer’s `PATCH_SHA256` and explicit test-selection lists. Enable local config only after successful installation; existing renderer processes cannot acquire new code through config reload.

## Validation gaps
- Add tint-only/all-backgrounds-off coverage; theme/host-color changes without pane output; zero-percent identity; repeated cached frames without cumulative blending.
- Assert reverse-video behavior, unchanged hyperlinks/underline metadata, protected image cells and wide-cell continuations. Check occluding panes/overlays remain untouched.
- Use isolated test sessions. Distinguish installed provenance from live activation; do not restart or replace existing clients to demonstrate completion.

## Recommended revision
1. Retain fresh pinned checkout and config work; settle the color-resolution and reverse-video contract first.
2. Implement independent tint gating, fill ordering and complete cache dependencies; retain the planned fullscreen fallback.
